key_insight: Global relaxed entropy-energy states can be constructed for dynamic thermoplasticity even when the temperature-dependent yield set collapses, but macroscopic Prandtl–Reuss normality is not guaranteed.
engineering_relevance: The analysis clarifies what constitutive behavior remains mathematically justified when modeling temperature-driven loss of plastic strength without viscosity or hardening.
method: Use a one-parameter Temam–Norton–Hoff–Galerkin approximation with an undiscretized heat equation.
Establish strong compactness of logarithmic temperature and entropy-weighted overstress estimates.
Represent constitutive limits through weighted measures and fibre lifts preserving exact normality and maximum plastic work.
evidence_signal: Analytical evidence includes an O(√(log n/n)) overstress convergence rate and an explicit smooth counterexample showing that intrinsic relaxed balances do not imply macroscopic normality.
watch_item: Available compactness does not identify a canonical macroscopic stress–plastic-flow pairing; under full yield collapse, plastic flow may fail to be a finite measure.
paper_title: Dynamic Prandtl-Reuss Thermoplasticity with Degenerating Yield Constraints
